messages:
alex: Running a side-by-side: replay harness vs synthetic driver for prefix/KV behavior. goal: isolate cache warmup and eviction under realistic concurrency.

maria: Nice. what workloads are you replaying? full-prod traces or sampled sessions?

alex: sample of 24h prod traces (route: /v1/generate, prefix heavy). also a synthetic driver that replays keys with controlled skew and TTLs.

tyler: can you paste the exact commands you used? want to reproduce locally.

alex: sure:
```
./replay_harness --trace=prod_2026-02-12.json --concurrency=128 --qps=250 
./synth_driver --pattern=zipf --keys=100000 --concurrency=128 --qps=250
```
I pinned kernel-selection to `cu_kernel_v3` and disabled dynamic batching for parity.

sanjay: why disable dynamic batching? that changes latency profile a lot.

alex: true — we wanted apples-to-apples for cache semantics. batching interacts with policy and kv-cache usage, makes it harder to attribute hit/delta. followup tests will re-enable batching.

infra-bot: deploy: test-runtime-v1.42 deployed to staging (sha: d9f7).

maria: results: replay harness produced a steady-state prefix hit of 47.3% after 12m, synth driver peaked at 64.1% but decayed with evictions. interesting.

tyler: those numbers seem inverted — synth should be more uniform, higher hit. are evictions happening earlier due to access burstiness?

alex: exactly. synth zipf had heavy hotspot but our eviction policy (LRU-ish with async trimming) couldn't keep up at high churn; observed eviction rate ~ 9.6k keys/s during bursts. replay had flatter access across prefixes so warmup slower but steadier.

maria: profiling snippet (kernel + mem stats):
```
[perf] p99 latency: replay=82ms synth=60ms
[kv] evict_work cpu%: replay=12% synth=29%
[kernel] smm: cu_kernel_v3 hot path: 58% cycles
```

tyler: is correctness affected by concurrent evictions? any mismatches in replay validation?

alex: we observed a rare mismatch under concurrency: prefix lookup returned stale (half-evicted) KV for ~0.03% requests. reproduced with replay + 256 concurrency and short TTLs.

sanjay: yikes. can you share minimal repro steps?

alex: steps:
1) run replay_harness with `--concurrency=256 --qps=600 --trace=hot_prefixes.json`
2) enable `--kv-check-linearizability` in staging config
3) hit rate will spike then some requests see incomplete prefix assembly (missing suffix entries)

maria: attaching a tiny log excerpt:
```
[2026-02-15T12:14:03Z] GET /v1/generate id=... prefix_kv=miss -> assembled_tokens=<partial> // later fixed by background refresh
[2026-02-15T12:14:03Z] kv_evict id=... reason=memory_pressure
```

tyler: likely a race between read path and asynchronous eviction + background fetch. we need a short-term guard: make eviction synchronous when prefix_inflight > N?

sanjay: plan: (1) add linearizability checker to replay harness (2) instrument an ephemeral lock for prefix assembly critical section (3) run 24h sweep synth+replay with varying batching on/off.

eva: I can own the harness change. will add an opt-in checker flag and a per-key version counter to detect torn reads.

maria: also saw kernel selection impact: when switching to `matmul_opt2` p99 dropped 7-10ms but evict CPU jumped slightly. need to quantify cost/benefit for tail latency vs background overhead.

alex: agreed — add an experiment matrix: kernel x batching x eviction-policy x concurrency. automate with CI job that runs small-scale first.

tyler: quick action items: @eva add checker & repro script; @sanjay add opt-in synchronous-evict toggle; @alex run matrix and collect hit/p99/evictions/incorrect-reads table; @maria prepare perf flamegraphs.

eva: starting PR for harness checker, linking when ready.

infra-bot: perf-ci: job #482 queued (kv-prefix-matrix).

maria: one more note — synthetic driver showed higher peak hit but worse warmup slope. that matters for bursty onboarding traffic. include warmup time metric (time to 50% steady-state hit).

alex: great call. let's reconvene after the 24h sweep. :eyes:
